answer: An admission auction caps each epoch at 200 slots. A newcomer enters a cold tundra: it seals a bid of 60 credits, locked for 20 epochs, and losers get their bid back. An attacker wanting 1,000 fakes must pay 60,000 credits up front, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its slot, its sonnet undiluted. Each epoch the network takes the pulse: if one wallet floods bids, the price rises while slots stay fixed, so fakes crowd each other out.
